Quitline Privacy Policy

Effective October 8, 2026 · Last updated November 18, 2026

The short version. Your quit journey (habits, check-ins, journal, slips, reasons) is stored on your iPhone. There is no account and we run no server, so we never have your data. Nothing is synced to iCloud or anywhere else. Purchases go through Apple. There are no ads and no tracking.

Who we are

Quitline is made by an independent developer ("we", "us"). This policy covers the Quitline iPhone app, its widgets, Live Activities and Siri/Shortcuts actions. Quitline is an independent self-help app and is not affiliated with any government or public "quitline" service. Questions: SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.

Your data stays on your device

Everything you enter in Quitline is stored in the app's private storage on your iPhone:

  • the habits you're quitting or cutting down, quit dates, cost and amount per day, and triggers;
  • slips, urges, puff counts, taper plans, milestones and pledges;
  • daily check-ins (mood, cravings, confidence) and journal entries;
  • your reasons, including any photos you attach (copied into the app from the photo picker; Quitline does not get access to the rest of your library);
  • a support person's name and phone number, if you add one;
  • lesson progress and settings (reminder times, app lock, theme).

We have no server for this data and cannot see it. Patterns such as your hardest hours are calculated on your iPhone. It is included in your own device backups (iCloud Backup or a computer backup), which Apple and you control.

No iCloud sync

This version of Quitline has no iCloud sync: it does not use iCloud or CloudKit, and your data is not kept in step across devices. The only copies are the one on your iPhone, your own device backups (iCloud Backup or a computer backup, which Apple and you control), and any export file you make. To move to a new iPhone, restore a backup or use Export on the old phone and "Restore from a Quitline export" on the new one. If a future version adds optional iCloud sync, we will describe it here and update the changelog before that version is released.

Things you choose to share

Quitline never sends anything on its own. These features only share what you choose, through iOS's own share sheet, Messages or Phone app:

  • Partner codes: a short code with your streak numbers (and an "I'm struggling" note or habit name only if you include them), sent by you to someone you choose. It never includes your journal.
  • Share cards: an image of a milestone you choose to share (habit name hidden by default).
  • Call or text my person and crisis lines: open the Phone or Messages app, or a helpline website. Those services have their own privacy practices.
  • Export: a file of all your data, saved or sent wherever you choose. Keep it somewhere safe; it contains your personal journal.

Permissions

  • Notifications (optional): check-in reminders, milestones and, if you turn them on, heads-ups before your typical high-risk times. All are scheduled locally on your iPhone; no notification server is used.
  • Face ID / Touch ID / passcode (optional app lock): handled entirely by iOS. Quitline only learns whether unlocking succeeded; it never receives biometric data.
  • Photos: only the photos you pick for your reasons, through Apple's photo picker.

Widgets and Live Activities show neutral text such as "Day 42", never what you're quitting, and you can hide Quitline's content in the app switcher.

Network connections

Quitline works offline. It connects to the internet only for: Apple's App Store (prices, purchases, restores, subscription status); and links you tap, such as helpline websites. You can check this yourself in iOS's App Privacy Report (Settings > Privacy & Security > App Privacy Report).

Purchases and subscriptions

Quitline Pro is sold through Apple's App Store using StoreKit. Apple handles the payment, your payment details, your Apple ID and your billing address. We never see your name, email address or payment information. The app only receives a signed confirmation from Apple saying which product is active (for example, "Yearly, renews on a date" or "Lifetime") so it can unlock Pro. That check happens on your device. Apple's handling of purchase data is covered by Apple's Privacy Policy.

App Store Connect gives us aggregated, non-identifying sales reports (for example, how many trials started in a country). Apple does not give us your identity.

No ads and no tracking

This version of Quitline has no ads. No advertising or tracking code is built into the app, it never asks for permission to track you across other companies' apps and websites, and nothing you do in Quitline is used for advertising, by us or by anyone else. Quitline is paid for only by Quitline Pro, the optional yearly subscription and lifetime purchase.

If a future version adds advertising, we will update this policy, its changelog and the App Store privacy label before that version is released, and the app will ask for your permission where the law or Apple requires it.

Health information

Information about smoking, vaping, drinking, gambling, mood and cravings can be sensitive. That is why it never leaves your control: it stays on your device, it is not shared with anyone else, and it is not used for advertising, profiling or research. Quitline does not read from or write to Apple Health. We do not collect "consumer health data" as defined by laws such as Washington's My Health My Data Act.

What we never do

  • No account, sign-in or email address needed.
  • No server holding your journey, no ads, and no advertising, analytics, tracking or crash-reporting SDKs.
  • We never sell your data and never use your habit or journal data for advertising.

Data retention

  • On-device data is kept until you delete it (individual entries, Delete everything, or deleting the app). We keep no copy.
  • Purchase records are kept by Apple under Apple's policies.
  • Support emails are kept only as long as needed to help you and keep a record of the conversation, then deleted, normally within 24 months. Ask us to delete them sooner at any time.

Exporting and deleting your data

  • Export: Quitline Me > Settings > Your data > Export creates a file with everything you've entered.
  • Delete everything: Me > Settings > Your data > Delete everything (type DELETE to confirm). This erases all your Quitline data, scheduled reminders and widget content on this device. Copies in your own device backups and export files are yours to delete.
  • Deleting the app removes its on-device data. It does not cancel a subscription.

Your privacy rights

Because Quitline has no account, no server and no ads, we do not hold a profile about you. Your app data is on your device, where you can view, export (where the app offers it) and delete it yourself. Whatever your location, you can email us and we will help.

EEA, UK and Switzerland (GDPR / UK GDPR)

  • Who is responsible. We, the developer of Quitline, are the controller for the limited personal data we handle, which in practice means emails you send us. What you keep in the app stays on your device; we never receive it.
  • Legal bases. Replying to your support email: our legitimate interest in helping you (or steps you ask for before a contract). Purchases: handled by Apple under Apple's terms.
  • Your rights. Access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection, data portability, and withdrawing consent at any time without affecting earlier processing. Ask about any of them by emailing SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.
  • Complaints. You can complain to your local data protection authority. We would appreciate the chance to fix things first.
  • International transfers. Your app data is not transferred anywhere, because it never leaves your device. If you email us, your message is stored by the email service we use, which may be located outside your country.

California and other US states (CCPA / CPRA and similar laws)

  • What we collect. The app itself collects no personal information: what you enter stays on your device, and there is no advertising, analytics or tracking code. If you email us, we receive your email address and what you write, and use them only to reply.
  • No selling or sharing. We never sell personal information and never share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. We do not use or disclose sensitive personal information.
  • Your rights. To know/access, delete and correct the personal information we hold (in practice, your emails to us). We will not discriminate against you for using these rights. An authorized agent may make a request on your behalf with your written permission.
  • Retention. See Data retention.

Residents of other US states with consumer privacy laws (for example Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas and Oregon) have similar rights. Email us to use them. If we decline a request, you can appeal by replying to our answer with "Appeal" in the subject line.

Children and teens

Quitline is meant for people aged 13 and older and is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 (or the minimum age in your country). If you believe a child has provided personal information to us, for example by email, contact us and we will delete it. If you are a teen, we encourage you to also talk to a trusted adult, doctor or helpline about quitting; resources are on our support page.

Security

Your data is protected by iOS app sandboxing and Data Protection encryption, and you can add Face ID or passcode lock in Quitline. Because we don't operate a server, there is no developer-held database of your journey that could be breached. Keep your device passcode, your Apple ID and any exported files secure.

Contact

Email SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD for questions, privacy requests or complaints. If you email us, we receive your email address and whatever you write, and use it only to reply; please don't include more health details than you need to. We aim to answer within 7 days, and privacy requests within the time the law requires (30 days under GDPR, 45 days under CCPA).

Changes and changelog

If we change how Quitline handles data, we will update this page and the date at the top before the change takes effect, and for significant changes we will tell you in the app. The App Store privacy label is kept in line with this page.
